summary.text: Saint Basil was Bishop of Murom and Ryazan. His ecclesiastical life connects him with the Murom icon and recounts his departure from Murom after slander.

blocks.text: The OCA distinguishes this hierarch, Basil I, from a later Bishop Basil II. It says he appears in the Laurentian Chronicles and in an early list of Ryazan bishops.

blocks.text: According to the received account, people in Murom falsely accused him of misconduct. He departed carrying an icon of the Theotokos. The life recounts his miraculous passage along the Oka River on his episcopal mantle and his welcome at Ryazan.
blocks.locator: Traditional account of accusations, Oka journey and reception at Ryazan

blocks.text: The source gives July 3, 1295, as Saint Basil’s death. His relics were uncovered and transferred on June 10, 1609. It records a bishop’s repose, not martyrdom.

blocks.text: Local veneration preceded the recovery of his relics. A sixteenth-century monk wrote an account of him around 1540. The cited source records commemorations on July 3 and June 10; its miracle narrative is distinct from the chronicle reference.
